title: Pointwise upper bound descends to the integral
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite probability space, and let $f : \Omega \to \bbr$ be a function satisfying $f(\omega) \le c$ for every $\omega \in \Omega$, where $c \in \bbr$ is a constant. Then the integral of $f$ with respect to the probability measure on $\Omega$ satisfies $\int_\Omega f \le c$.
hypotheses_covered: Ω is a finite probability space
f is a real-valued function on Ω
replaced:
If $f : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfies $f(\omega) \le c$ for all $\omega$ in a
finite probability space, then $\int_\Omega f \le c$.
